order: Generate a what-if video prompt that results in something very high quality (Commander, via Claude Code)

pitches.title: What if the air *vanished* for 5 seconds?
pitches.cover: WITHOUT AIR, A JET WOULD FALL 122 M IN 5 SECONDS
pitches.frame1: A sunny city plaza at lunchtime: fountain, pigeons, cafe tables, cars on the avenue. Counter: AIR VANISHES IN · 03.000 · SEA-LEVEL AIR: 101 KPA. Title: What if the air vanished for 5 seconds?

beats.what: Every sound cuts out at once. The blue sky drains to black with stars at noon. Pigeons drop like stones. The fountain's water erupts into white boiling foam.
Coffee and drinks foam and boil over in their cups. People clutch their ears (mid-distance, no faces).
The whole sea fizzes white to the horizon under a black sky. The Sun is a hard white disc with no glow.
An airliner's engines flame out. It falls silently through a cloud deck that is evaporating to nothing.
Earth's blue rim vanishes and the clouds disappear: the planet looks airless, like the Moon.
AIR RETURNS 00.000: a planet-wide thunderclap. A shock ring rolls across the plaza, windows flex, every pigeon bursts back into the air.
The blue rim snaps back around the whole planet, and a white shock-front ring races around the globe. End card, then a hard cut to frame 1.
beats.counter: 5 SECONDS · EVERY SOUND ON EARTH STOPPED

pitches.law: Air vanishes for 5 s: pressure 101.3 kPa → 0. Water boils whenever pressure < its vapour pressure (2.33 kPa at 20 °C), so every open water surface boils at room temperature. With no air there is no lift, so everything flying is in free fall: ½·9.81·5² = 122.6 m in 5 s. No air = no sound. No scattering = black sky with stars at noon.
pitches.dramatization: The air disappears and reappears in an instant. The return is shown as a planet-wide thunderclap (the one liberty).
why: Fresh in our niche: the hits are 'what if X vanished for 5 seconds' (Clover protons: 465.8K likes), but air hasn't been done in our lane (verify before posting).
Matches the taste profile: chaos on screen by 0:03, five locations (city → cafe → bay → sky → orbit), and planes in trouble.
Every beat reuses a finished set: city plaza, bay, cloud deck + airliner, Earth from orbit.
The cover is a verifiable number (122.6 m), the same free-fall law viewers can check.
pitches.risk: Showing 'nothing' is hard. Every beat must show a visible effect (boiling, falling, black sky). The return thunderclap and the shock ring are the payoff, so build them first and check them at phone size.
